Strikethrough Text Generator

The only way to cross something out where there is no format button

Effects & Glitch
  • Strikethrough
  • Underline
  • Double Underline
  • Slashed
  • Overline
  • Upside-Down / Flip

A line through the text, drawn by the characters themselves

A price with a line through it says more than the word sale ever does, and in a field with no formatting button there is exactly one way to draw that line: U+0336, the combining long stroke overlay, appended after every character. The stroke is drawn across whatever it lands on, so the effect goes wherever the text goes. Spaces are skipped here, which is why the line breaks between words rather than running one unbroken rule across the phrase.

The arithmetic catches people out. Because each stroke is its own character sitting invisibly behind a letter, a ten-letter word costs twenty characters against a bio limit, and the counter offers no hint as to why. Nothing you can see accounts for the missing room. That aside, it is the most portable trick on the site: no styling is involved, only extra characters, so an edited message or a finished item on a list keeps its stroke through every copy.

Also searched as: crossed out text, line through text, cross out generator.

Where Strikethrough text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks anywhere plain text goes, and is the only way to strike through or underline in a field that will not take formatting. Watch outEach mark is its own character, so the length counts against a bio limit even though nothing extra is visible. A few platforms strip combining marks on save.

Strikethrough questions

Why does my bio say I am over the limit?

Because the stroke is a character. Every letter you can see is followed by an invisible one that the counter includes, so a forty-character line arrives as eighty. Nothing on screen explains the gap. If a field is tight, strike only the words that need it and leave the rest untouched.

Can I cross out just one word in a sentence?

Yes, and it usually reads better than striking the whole line. Convert only the word or figure you want crossed, paste it back where it belongs, and type the rest normally. That is how an old price sitting beside a new one works, and how a correction stays visible in an edited post.

Why does the line stop at every space?

This site skips spaces deliberately, so each word gets its own stroke and the gaps stay open. A continuous rule across a phrase means striking the spaces too, which some fonts handle awkwardly. Word by word also survives wrapping better, since a line break falls in a gap rather than mid-stroke.
